bottom_line: In TOPCAT, spironolactone vs placebo did not significantly reduce the primary composite outcome (hazard ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.77 to 1.04).
implications: These results support that spironolactone, as tested, did not significantly reduce the primary composite outcome versus placebo (hazard ratio, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.77–1.04; P=0.14). The data do support a lower incidence of hospitalization for heart failure (206 patients [12.0%] vs. 245 patients [14.2%]; hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.69–0.99; P=0.04), while showing higher hyperkalemia (18.7% vs. 9.1%) and more frequent doubling of serum creatinine (10.2% vs. 7.0%) with spironolactone.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind trial in HFpEF comparing spironolactone vs placebo.
major_points.quote: In this randomized, double-blind trial, we assigned 3445 patients with symptomatic heart failure and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 45% or more to receive either spironolactone (15 to 45 mg daily) or placebo.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death, aborted cardiac arrest, or hospitalization for HF management.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, aborted cardiac arrest, or hospitalization for the management of heart failure.

major_points.text: Hyperkalemia was more frequent with spironolactone; hypokalemia was less frequent.
major_points.quote: The spironolactone group had a higher rate of hyperkalemia (18.7%, vs. 9.1% in the placebo group) and a lower rate of hypokalemia (16.2% vs. 22.9%).

major_points.text: A substantial proportion permanently discontinued study drug in both groups.
major_points.quote: There were 590 participants in the spironolactone group (34.3%) and 541 in the placebo group (31.4%) who permanently discontinued the study drug while continuing to be followed for study outcomes.
